FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Assembly Hand Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1962 and its first revision was taken up in 1972 after .incorpcmting following changes: a) b) c) Minimum values of hardness were specified, Tolerance limits were modified, and Sampling plans were also modified.

While second revision was taken up in 1985, this standard was split up as: IS 1931 Spec~lcation for files: Part Part Part Part Part 1 2 3 4 5 Technical supply conditions Engineer's tiles Saw files Mill files Special purpose files

In this revision, the followlng changes have been made: a) The endurance tcst rcqui rements have been limited to bastard cut of engineer's files only. The number of strokes for stock removal has been reduced to minimize the time taken for testing the files for endurance test, Dimensions of hand profcr have been incorporated for guidance only, Figure showing the usc of hand prover has also been included, and Micro hardness testing has been made as a type test.

b) c) d)

While revising this standard, all the five parts have been combined into a single comprehensive standard. The files which arc indicated in (l\c Tables, 1, 2, 4, 9, 10 and 14 are wideIy used for forestry work, The nccdlc tiles have been covcrcd in IS 3152:1980 `Specification for needle files (fir.r[ revision)' and the rasps have been covered in IS 3587: 1985 `Specification for rasps (second revision)'. The files used by instrument makers, jewellers and dic sinkers. as well as high speed steel files have not been covered in the above specification. While preparing this standard, considerable assistance has been derived from the following standards: 1S0 234/1 : 1983 1S0 234/2 BS 498 : 1982 : 1990 Files and rasps -- Part 1 : Dimensions Files and rasps -- Part 2: Characteristics of cut issued by the International Organization for Standardization (1S0) Specification for rasps and engineers' files issued by the British Standards Institution (UK)

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 1S 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in [he rounded off value should bc lhc same as that of the specified value in this standard.

A file or rasp is considered mpcrcd when L1is between 25 and 50 percent of length 1. and the dimensions of the point b, and d, do not exceed 80 percent of the dimensions of b and d respectively. On tapered files and rasps the taper length L, is measured from the point to the parallel part of the tile or rasp. 4 CUTS 4.1 There shall be four grades of cuts, namely, bastard, second cut, smooth and dead smooth. The number of cuts shall be measured along the centre line of the file. 4.2 There shall be two types of cuts for the files: a) b) Single cut, and Double cut.

5 TYPES 5.1 The engineer's files shall be of the following types: a) Flat files, b) Hand files, c) Half round files, d) Round tiles, e) $ Square files, Three square tiles,

g) Warding files, h) Knife files, and j) Feather edge files.

5.2 The saw files shall be of the following types: a) Taper saw files, b) Band saw taper regular files, c) Blunt hand saw tiles, d) Double ended saw files, e) Pit saw fdes, t) Cant saw files, and

4.2.1 Single Cut Single cut shall mean a set of parallel cuts on lhc surface, except where otherwise specified (see Fig. 2). 4.2.2 Double Cut Double cut shall mean two sets of parallel cuts on the surface, one of which shall cross the other. The first cut and the second cut are called over cut and up cut respectively (see Fig. 2). Where the files are double cut, the number of cuts per centimetre shall relate to the number of up cuts pcr centimetre. 4.3 Other types of cuts, like wavy cut, curved cut, which are also in use, shall be permitted as special requirement subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.4 Details of the cut, such as single or double cut, aud number of cuts per cenlimctre applicable to files of different types shall be as given in the relevant Tables. 4.5 Safe Edges Those edges of the files which are not cut and are left smooth, shall be called safe edges.

g) Cross cut saw files. 5.3 The mill files shall be of the following types: a) Taper mill fil~ b) Parallel mill filcx+ and c) Blunt heavy mill files. 5.4 The speeial purpose files shall be of the following types: a) Hand finishing files, b) Cabinet tiles, c) Reaper files, and d) Block files.

Material

The material for the manufacture of files and handprover shall be normally of designation 118 T3 or 133 T3 according to IS 3748 or any suitable alloy steel.

Hardness

The hardness of the cutting portion of the files shall be 745 HV (=62 HRC), Min on the tip of the teeth as measured by the micro hardness tester. 7 Dimensions AND SHAPES

7.1 Engineer's Files 7.1.1 Flat Files
7.1.1.1 The dimensions of the flat files shall be as

7.1.5.2 Square files shall be of square cros.+section, parallel for approximately two-thirds tile length and then tapering towards the point. All sides shall have double cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.
7.1.6

Three Square Files

given in Table 1. 7.1.1.2 Flat files shall be of rectangular cross-section, parallel for approximately two-thirds file length and then tapering towards the point in width and parallel or slightly tapering in thickness. Both edges may be either square or -round. The sides shall have double cut, whereas the edges shall have single cut. 7.1.2 Hand Files
7.1.2.1 The dimensions of the hand files shall be as

7.1.6.1 The dimensions of the three square files shall be as given in Table 6.

Three square files shall be of equilateral triangular cross-sectio% parallel for approximately twothirds file length and then tapering towards the point. All sides shall have double cut. The edges shall be uncut or cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.
7.1.6.2 7.1.7

Warding Files

given in Table 2. 7.1.2.2 Hand files shall be of wtangular cross-seetio~ and paratlel in width throughout. These shall be paratlel in thickness for approximately two-thirds file length and rest tapering towards the point. Both edges may be either square or round. The-sides shall have double cut. One edge shall be of sing]e cut, whereas the other shall be the safe edge. 7.1.3 Half Round Files 7.1.3.1 The dimensions of the half round files shall be as given in Table 3. 7.1.3.2 Half round files shall be of one side flat and other convex cross-section, parallel for approximately two-thirds file length towards the point in width and then parallel or slightly tapering in thickness. Flat side for files of all grades of cut, shall have double cut. The convex side shall have double cut for bastard files, single cut or double cut for second cut files and single cut or double cut for smooth files. Files shall have cuts up to the point. 7.1.4 Round Files
7.1.4.1 The dimensions of the round files shall be as

7.1.7.1 The dimensions of the warding files shall be as given in Table 7.

Warding files shall be of rectangular crossscction, parallel in thickness throughout, parallel in width for approximately two-thirds file length and then tapering towards the point. The sides shall have double cut, whereas the edges shall have single cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.
7.1.7.2

7.1.8 Knife Files
7.1.8.1 The dimensions of the knife tiles shall be as given in Table 8.

7.1.8.2 Knife files shall be of uniform wedge cross-section, having the thinner edge straight, thicker edge parallel to the thinner edge for approximately twothirds file length and then tapering towards the point. The sides shall have double cut. The thinner edge shall have single cut, whereas the thicker edge shall be left uncut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.
7.1.9 Feather Edge Files

given in Table 4. 7.1.4.2 Round files shall be of circular cross-section, parallel for approximately two-thirds tile length and then tapering towards the point. Baslard files less than 150 mm in length shall have single cut (preferably of 3

The dimensions of the feather edge files shall be as given in Table 9.
7.1.9.1

7.1.9.2 Feather edge, files shall be of elongated diamond cross-seetio~ parallel in width and thickness throughout. All -sides shall have single cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.

as given in Table 10. 7.2.1.2 Taper saw files shall be of equilateral triangular cross-sectiou parallel for approximately two-thirds file length and then tapering towards the point. 7.2.5 Pit Saw Files
7.2,5.1 The dimensions of the pit saw files shall be as given in Table 14.

cross-section having an obtuse apex angle, parallel in width and thickness throughout. The base angles shall be flattened and cut. The sides and edges shall have single cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point. 7.2.7 Cross Cut Saw Files
7.2.7.1 The dimensions of the cross cut saw tiles shall be as given in Table 16.

7.2.5.2 Pit saw files shallbe of one side fl@ and other convex cross-section, parallel in width and thickness Throughout. Both flat and convex sides shall have single cut. Point shall be left uncut. 7.2.6 Cant Saw Files

as given in Table 15. 7.2.6.2 Cant saw files shall be of isosceles triangular

7.2.7.2 Cross cut saw files shall be of uniform wedge cross-section, with the thicker edge having convex shape. The sides and the edges shall have single cut. Files shall have cuts up to the point.

7.3 Mill Files 7.3.1 Taper Mill Files
7.3.1.1 The dimensions of the taper mill files shall be as given in Table 17. 7.3.1.2 Taper mill tiles shall be of rectangular crossscction, parallel for approximately two-thirds file length and then tapering towards (he point in width and thickness. The edges may be either two square edges, one round edge and other square or two round edges. Sides and edges shall have single cut. Point shall be left uncut.

7.3.2.2 Parallel mill files shall be of rectangular crosssection, parallel in width and thickness throughout. The edges may be either two square edges, one round edge and other square, or two round edges. Sides and edges shall have single cut. Point shall be left uncut. 7.3.3 Blunt Heavy Mill Files
7.3.3.1 The dimensions of the blunt heavy mill files

shall be as given in Table 19. 7.3.3.2 Blunt heavy mill files shall be of rectmqgdar cross-section, parallel in width and thickness throughout. The edges may be either one round edge and other square or two round edges. Sides and edges shall have single cut. Point shall be left uncut.

1s 1931:2000 12.1 For dimensions and visual inspection, a single sampling plan with inspection level III and AQL of 2.5 pement as given in Tables I and IIA of IS 2500 (Part 1) shall be followed.

12.2 For warpage test, distortion test and hand prover tcs~ a single sampling plan with inspection level I and AQL of 2.5 percent as given in Tables I and H A of IS 2500( Part 1) shall be followed. 12.3 For endurance test, one sample from a lot of 3000 or part thereof shall bc selected. After the test, it shall meet the requirements laid down in relevant Tables. 13 TESTS 13.1 Warpage Test Warpage is the angular displacement between the plane of Ihe side at shoulder and at the point. Warpage shall be measured by means of an instrument consisting of one horizontal surface and one pivoted surface to which an indicating pointer is attached, supported on a master flat surface. A typical instrument used for warpage testing is given in Fig. 4. The horizontal surface shall be adjustable so .as to accommodate the length of the file under test, The shoulder shall be

pressed against the horizontal surface, the pivoted surface shall then be rotated in its pivot to bear on the side of the point. The warpage shall be indicated by a pointer on a scale graduated in degrees. The files shall meet the requirements of warpage specified in the relevant Tables.
13.2

Distortion Test

The distortion shall be considered as the deviation of the centre line of file from a straight line. It is half the difference between maximum and minimum gauge readings taken on opposite sides. The distortion shall be measured by means of a diat gauge and two steel blocks supported on a master flat surface. A typical instrument for measuring distortion is given in Fig. 5. Flat blocks shall be employed for flat surface files and V-blocks for round and cuwed surface files. The flat or V-blocks shall be placed under the point and the shoulder of the file under test. The-dial gauge readings shall be taken in the middle of nominal length at opposite sides by rotating the files through 180� around the centre line .of the file. The files shall meet the requirements of distortion specified in relevant Tables.

13.3 Hand Prover Test (Routine Test)
13.3.1 The hardness of hand prover for testing different files shall be as given below:

a) For sawfdes615 HV A4in or 56 HRC Mln, and b) For other files 545 HV A4in or 52 HRCA4in. 13.3.2 The prover may be of cross-seetion 25 mm x -5 mm and having length approximately 250 mm for the convenience of proper grip. The prover shall be

applied to the file at an angle of approximately 30� (see Fig. 6) and firmly over the tile from point to shoulder using only pressure sufficient to make it bite. The files shall eut without any signs of slip, blunting or stripping of teeth. Any file that allows the prover to slip over any portion of its surface shall be considered unsatisfaeto~ and shall be rejeeted.
NOTE -- The word `slip' in the above
absence of noticeable abrading the prover and absence of bite. requirement means cutting or "filing action on

K

FIG. 6 HAND PROVER TEST

26

IS 1931:2000 13.4 Micro Hardness Test (~pe Test) Files shall be checked for hardness requirements speciiled in 6, by mireo hardness tester. Two numbers of files of each type shall be checked every quarter of the year to evalu~te the quality control at the manufacturing process. 13.5 Endurance Test This test shall be applicable only to the engineer's files which are of double cut types and have bastard grade of cut. This test shall apply only to the flat sides of file. This test shall not be conducted on files of second cut, smooth and dead smooth grades of cut. This will also not be applicable to single cut type of files. The endurance test requirements as laid down in relevant Tables shrdl be met. 13.5.1 The test bar on which the file is to be tested shall beof25mm X25nunor12mm x25mminerosssection depending upon the width of file under test. The test bars shall be of 60T6 steel with the sulphur and phosphorous content not exceeding 0.06 pereent each (see IS 3748). The test bar shall have a hardness value between 220 to 230 W.
13.5.2 The file testing machine shall be operated at a frequency of 50 to 55 strokes per minute. The length of stroke shall be adjusted to 150 mm. The file shall exert a constant pressure of about 20 N/cm2 (2 kgfkmz approx) on the test bar during the entire test. It shall be so arranged that the file works flat and relieves the test bar during the return stroke.

A taper saw extra slim file with grade of cut as second cut (SC) having nominal length L = 125 mm shall be designated as: Taper Saw Extm Slim File SC 125 -- IS 1931 A blunt heavy mill -file with grade of cut bastard having nominal length L = 200 mm and with two round edges shall be designated as: Blunt Heavy Mill File -- B -- Two Round Edges 200 -- IS 1931 A cabinet file with grade of cut bastard, having nominal length L = 250 u shall be designated as: Cabinet File B 250 -- IS 1931 15 PRESERVATIVE ~AND
PACKING

15.1 The files may be given a suitable rust preventive treatment before packing.

15.2 Unless otherwise agreed upon by the manufacturer and the purchaser, files shall be individually wrapped in wax paper to avoid damage to the teeth and to proteet them against corrosion. They shall be then packed in cardboard boxes. Each box shall contain files of similar type, eut and length.
16 MARKING 16.1 Each file shall be stamped legibIy with nominal size, the grade of cut and the manufacturer's name/ initials or trade-mark on the uncut portion of the file but in case where the space is limited, the tang may also be used for the purpose.

13.5.3 The minimum length of test bar filed away by a flat side of the file, at 30000 strokes, shallbe not less than the limits specified in the relevant Tables. 13.5.3.1 During the endurance test of files, the following conditions shall be kept in view: a) The test bar and the tile under test shall be kept free from oil: and

16.1.1 When the space does not permit the marking of grade of cut in fill, the following abbreviations may be used: Bastard (B), Second Cut (SC),, Smooth (S), D=d Smooth (DS)
16.2 Boxes in which files are packed shall also be labelled or marked to show the description of size and quantity, in accordance with the best trade practices.

b) During the test, files shall be cleaned once during 1000 strokes. 14 DESIGNATION The files shall be designated by commonly used names, grade of cw nominal file length (excluding the tang), details of edges (wherever applicable) and number of Indian Standards.

The details of conditions under which the Iicence for the use of Standard Mark maybe granted to manufkturem or producers may be obtained from rhe Bureau of Indian Standards.
